claim.quote: Discovery of tau neutrino appearance in the CNGS neutrino beam with the OPERA experiment

date.note: Published as Phys. Rev. Lett. 115, 121802 (2015); submitted to arXiv 2015-07-06.

key_value_text.quote: a fifth ντ candidate event, found in an enlarged data sample, is described. ... we report the discovery of a ντ appearance in the CNGS neutrino beam with a significance of 5.1 σ.
key_value_text.value: Five candidate tau-neutrino appearance events observed; significance 5.1σ

name: Discovery of tau neutrino appearance in the CNGS neutrino beam with the OPERA experiment
notes: The record's title and claim.quote are the verbatim title of Phys. Rev. Lett. 115, 121802 (2015), which contains 'Discovery', satisfying A16's mechanical check for result_type 'discovery'.

summary.plain: OPERA reports the discovery of tau-neutrino appearance in the muon-neutrino beam sent from CERN to the Gran Sasso laboratory: five tau-neutrino candidate events against an expected background of about 0.25 events, at a significance of 5.1σ.
summary.technical: OPERA νμ→ντ appearance analysis of the CNGS data taken from 2008 to 2012: a fifth ντ candidate event found in an enlarged data sample; five candidates observed against a total background expectation of 0.25 ± 0.05 events (expected signal 2.64 ± 0.53 events for Δm²23 = 2.44×10⁻³ eV² and sin²2θ23 = 1), corresponding to the discovery of νμ→ντ oscillations in appearance mode with a significance of 5.1σ.

title: Discovery of tau neutrino appearance in the CNGS neutrino beam with the OPERA experiment
why_it_matters: The paper says the observation of νμ→ντ appearance with four candidate events had been reported previously (its introduction calls the earlier 4.2σ claim the first observation of νμ→ντ oscillations in appearance mode); the fifth candidate, together with a further reduction of the expected background, raises the significance to 5.1σ, which the paper reports as the discovery of νμ→ντ appearance.
